title: Orkney 2022, Kirkwall East (Scottish STV)
about: A real Scottish council ward, 5 candidates for 4 seats, counted by the Scottish rules: the ballots from MGGG's scot-elex collection.

title: Shetland 2017, ward 2 (QPQ)
about: A real Scottish council ward, 4 candidates for 3 seats, counted by Woodall's Quota Preferential by Quotient instead of the Scottish rules. Both elect the same three; choose the scottish ruleset under stv to compare the counts.

title: Maine 2018, 2nd congressional district (instant-runoff)
about: The first U.S. congressional race decided by ranked choice: 4 candidates, the two independents defeated together, Jared Golden elected. From FairVote's copy of the cast vote record; the count matches the State's every round.

title: Minneapolis 2021, mayor (Schulze)
about: 19 candidates and nearly 144,000 ballots ranking up to three, counted by Schulze's Condorcet method. The City's instant-runoff count elected Jacob Frey, whom Schulze ranks first too; choose the irv ruleset under stv to see that count.

title: Minneapolis 2021, Park Board at large (Minneapolis rules)
about: 8 candidates for 3 seats, counted by the City's multi-seat rules: fractional transfers truncated to 4 places, hopeless candidates defeated together before each surplus.

title: NSW 2024, Ballina B Ward (NSW councils' rules)
about: A New South Wales council ward, 7 candidates for 3 seats, counted by the NSW Electoral Commission's rules from its published ballot papers (identical papers merged).

title: ACT 2020, Brindabella (ACT Hare-Clark)
about: An electorate of the Australian Capital Territory's Legislative Assembly: 23 candidates for 5 seats, 55,413 ballot papers from Elections ACT's preference data. Every count matches the official distribution of preferences exactly, to the 6 decimal places the Act sets.

title: Portland 2024, City Council District 4 (Portland rules)
about: Portland, Oregon's first multi-seat council election: 30 candidates and a write-in line for 3 seats, 76,717 ballots from Multnomah County's cast vote record. Every round matches the County's to 4 decimal places.

title: Albany, CA 2024, City Council (Albany rules)
about: 5 candidates for 3 seats, from Alameda County's cast vote record (identical rankings merged), counted as the County's 2024 report does, every round matching.

title: Cambridge, MA 2013, School Committee (Cambridge STV)
about: 15 candidates for 6 seats, one line a ballot in the City's order: Cambridge STV moves whole ballots, a surplus's every n-th ballot, so the order matters.

title: MapLibre 2025, Governing Board (Meek)
about: A real election run by Meek's method on OpaVote: 6 candidates for 5 seats, 92 ballots (3 of them empty). The winners match OpaVote's.

title: Nauru 2019, Boe (Dowdall Borda)
about: Nauru's Dowdall Borda count, 5 candidates for 2 seats: ballots built to match the published table of ranks, so they reproduce the official scores.

title: Wikipedia's worked example (STV)
about: Andrea, Brad, Carter and Delilah for 2 seats, 57 voters: ballots rebuilt from the round totals of Wikipedia's "Counting single transferable votes" article.

title: ERS97's model election (ERS97 rules)
about: The Electoral Reform Society's worked model election from its 1997 rules ("How to conduct an election by the Single Transferable Vote"): 11 candidates for 6 seats.

title: A synthetic Senate count (Australian Senate rules)
about: Synthetic: 15 candidates for 5 seats, where surpluses move in order of election rather than largest first. Every count matches pyRCV2's Senate count of it.

title: A synthetic Victorian count (Victorian Legislative Council)
about: Synthetic: 10 candidates for 5 seats; C4 and C7 tie on 37 for exclusion, settled by the last count at which they differed. Every round matches OpenTally's Victorian preset (Victoria publishes no ballots).

title: A synthetic Western Australian count (WA Legislative Council)
about: Synthetic: 8 candidates for 4 seats; an excluded candidate's parcels move one at a time, in the order received. Every round matches OpenTally's Western Australian preset (WA publishes no ballots).

title: Where Warren and Meek differ (Warren)
about: A synthetic election, 8 candidates for 5 seats, from the checks against droop: Warren's method elects C2 for the last seat, Meek's C8. Switch the method to meek to compare.

title: A near-tie with a cycle (CPO-STV)
about: Synthetic: 8 candidates for 4 seats, 10,000 voters. Committees differing by one equally popular candidate beat each other in a cycle, which the beatpath completion settles.

title: Tideman's A53 (Schulze STV)
about: 10 candidates for 4 seats from Tideman's collection: the worked example of Schulze's paper.

title: Tideman's A53 as a party list (Schulze proportional)
about: The same election ranked place by place, as the paper's section 9.3 works it: J A G D F B E C I H.

title: Tied rankings (Meek)
about: Made up for the demo: 50 voters, some ranking candidates equally ("Ash=Cedar"), 2 seats; Meek's method splits a tied ballot between them.
